label: Pro 2.1.0
title: Run it as a service
lede: Pro 2.1.0 adds a standalone server, so apps in PHP, Python, Go or any other language can send webhooks through Vector over HTTP. It also adds outgoing regions with fixed IPs and delivery limits per tenant.

items.title: Standalone server in Docker
items.text: Run Vector as its own process with a REST API, a built-in delivery worker and an admin page. Your database holds everything, no Redis needed.

items.title: Send events from any language
items.text: Create an endpoint and post a message with plain HTTP. The receiver gets a signed Standard Webhooks request with retries.
items.codeTitle: Create an endpoint and send an event
items.code:
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/v1/endpoints \
  -H "authorization: Bearer $VECTOR_API_KEY" -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"url":"https://customer.example.com/hooks","tenant":"acme","eventTypes":["invoice.*"]}'

curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/v1/messages \
  -H "authorization: Bearer $VECTOR_API_KEY" -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"eventType":"invoice.paid","tenant":"acme","payload":{"id":"inv_1","amount":1200},"idempotencyKey":"inv_1"}'

items.title: Regions with a fixed outgoing IP
items.text: Send an endpoint's requests through a proxy with a fixed IP, so customers who allow-list your address get the region that matches. A region is an outgoing route, your data stays in one database.

items.title: Limits per tenant and endpoint
items.text: Stop one busy tenant from using all of a worker's capacity. Deliveries over the limit wait and are not counted as failed attempts.

items.title: Use the same controls in your own Node app
items.text: Already embedding Vector? createDeliveryControls gives you regions and limits as options for createVector, without the server.

note: The demo cannot show this: the server needs your own host, database and proxies. Limit counters live in the memory of each process.
